answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity in compute, not goodwill. Each epoch the network publishes a challenge beacon, and every identity must answer with fresh, original work before peers countersign it. Admission is gated by a proof-of-compute puzzle, so multiplying identities costs real CPU per head - a farm pays a thousandfold. Trust accrues slowly, like yarrow, to identities that keep answering; clones stay worth exactly their hashing cost. A missed epoch simply earns nothing, on a quartz-regular cadence. Flooding backfires: sybils split one pool, never multiply it.
